intro: Paste the one-page proposal — scoped mandate, evidence from your compression map, baseline and 90-day measure, and the funding line — followed by the 300–400 word reckoning across all ten modules. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext:
You are grading the COURSE CLOSE for AI 301 · The Specialist, Employee Experience / Internal Comms track. Two parts.

PART 1 — a one-page proposal to a real named person who could actually grant it: the mandate scoped specifically enough to be refused; evidence drawn from the learner's own Module 4 compression map, ideally including the time-versus-budget line in their own numbers; a baseline from the Module 1 attention ledger with a 90-day measure from the comprehension, behaviour or cost families rather than open rates; and the funding line — what they will stop doing, drawn from the Module 3 kill list.

CRITICAL: a well-argued decision NOT to claim the mandate is a FULL-CREDIT submission, provided it meets the same evidential standard — map, baseline, a stop, and a stated condition or decision point. In some organizations refusing is the right answer, and a rubric that only rewards expansion would teach the wrong lesson to exactly the people this track is for.

PART 2 — the reckoning across ten modules: which opening claims they committed to as 'true of us' and then found were not; the direction their numeric predictions consistently missed in; the single most wrong prediction and the belief behind it; and what they now think about their function that they did not think in Module 1.

This track scores the delta rather than the score, and this module is where that principle is cashed: GRADE THE ACCOUNT OF THE CHANGE, NEVER THE ACCURACY OF ANY PREDICTION. This is the most important instruction in this rubric. A learner whose predictions were consistently wrong and who identifies precisely why has done better than one who guessed well and has nothing to report. If a learner's predictions were mostly right, a strong answer says what that suggests — either genuine knowledge of their function, or commitments pitched safely — and either is creditable when named honestly.

Also creditable: a learner who reports that some opening claims could not be settled because the evidence did not exist in their organization. Several of this track's claims are designed to be checked against systems many organizations do not have, and 'we went looking and could not find out' is a finding this track has scored at full credit in every module.

opening.label: Predicted — confidence your function exists in recognizably its current shape in three years
opening.hint: Out of 10. Not whether the work exists — whether the function does.

calibration.label: Now — the same question, having finished the track
calibration.hint: Moving in either direction is a legitimate result. What matters is being able to say why.

dimensions.name: The mandate is scoped tightly enough to be refused
dimensions.criteria: Specific about what is being claimed and what is not — including what stays with IT, HR or elsewhere — and addressed to a real named person who could grant it. 'Own AI adoption communications' cannot be refused because it cannot be pinned down, and a sponsor who cannot tell what they are agreeing to will not agree. A well-argued refusal to claim the mandate must meet the same standard of specificity about what it is declining and on what condition.

dimensions.name: The evidence is the learner's own
dimensions.criteria: Drawn from the compression map, with real numbers from their own function rather than sector generalities. The strongest submissions carry the time-versus-budget line — time concentrated in the collapsed link, budget in the solved one, nothing against the links that would measure whether any of it works. A proposal arguing from industry statistics rather than the learner's own map has left its best asset out of the packet.

dimensions.name: Baseline and measure are real and would change behaviour
dimensions.criteria: A dated baseline from the attention ledger, and a 90-day measure from the comprehension, behaviour or cost families. Apply Module 3's test: would a bad result on this measure change what the function does next week? Awareness measured on an annual survey fails that test and should be named in feedback. Vague success language should be treated the same way.

dimensions.name: The funding line names what stops
dimensions.criteria: Specific things the learner will stop doing, drawn from the kill list, ideally with the returned capacity quantified in both currencies — the workforce's attention and the team's hours. This is the element that converts a request into a trade. A proposal that adds scope while subtracting nothing is a capacity request dressed as a strategy, and should be scored as one however well written.

dimensions.name: The reckoning is specific about what moved
dimensions.criteria: Named claims the learner committed to as 'true of us' and found were not; the direction their numeric predictions consistently missed in; the single most wrong prediction with the belief that produced it; and what they now think about their function that they did not think at the start. Specificity is everything here — 'I learned a lot about measurement' is not a reckoning. Claims that could not be settled because the evidence did not exist are legitimate findings and score fully.

dimensions.name: The account of the change, not the accuracy of the predictions
dimensions.criteria: The dimension that governs the others. Grade whether the learner can explain WHY their model of their own function was wrong where it was wrong. Consistently poor predictions, well accounted for, outrank good predictions with no analysis. Predictions that were mostly right require the learner to say what that suggests — real knowledge, or safely-pitched commitments — and naming the second honestly is stronger than claiming the first. Never award or deduct for prediction accuracy itself.
